plan: Second-price sealed-bid auction with independent private values and risk-neutral, rational opponents. Truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy: overbidding risks negative payoff if you win when the second-highest bid is between your value and your inflated bid; underbidding risks losing when winning would be profitable. With no usable history (single round), and values uniformly 0–49 with $0.1 granularity, maximization of expected profit dictates bidding exactly my value. Therefore, I bid 39.0 to win whenever the second-highest bid is below 39 and pay that second-highest bid, yielding nonnegative surplus.

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price auction with independent private values. The weakly dominant strategy is to bid my true value: overbidding risks paying above value; underbidding risks losing positive-surplus wins. With ties broken randomly, no deviation improves expected payoff. Therefore, I will bid exactly my value, $20.0, to maximize expected profit. ]

[ This is a sealed-bid second-price (Vickrey) auction with independent private values. The dominant strategy is to bid your true value, regardless of others’ strategies. Underbidding risks losing when you would have positive surplus; overbidding risks winning and paying more than your value if the second-highest bid exceeds your value. With value 20, bidding 20 maximizes expected profit and is strategically robust. No history to adjust for in round 1. ]
